svg.title: Prefrontal cortex as a meta-RL system
svg.text: Prefrontal cortex as a meta-RL system
Wang et al. 2018; Wang et al. 2016; Duan et al. 2016 (RL$^2$)
Algorithm
Prefrontal network = LSTM with weights $\theta$ and memory (activity) $h$
Input: observation $o_t$, plus its own last action $a_{t-1}$ and last reward $r_{t-1}$
Output: policy $\pi_\theta(a \mid h)$ (actor) and value $V_\theta(h)$ (critic)
Meta-environment: a new task every episode
$\tau \sim p(\tau)$, e.g. a two-armed bandit with random reward probabilities $p_L, p_R$
Memory $h$ is reset only at the start of an episode, never between trials
Repeat for every episode:
$\tau \sim p(\tau),\ \ h_0 = 0$
New task; clear the memory
Inner loop, every trial $t$: memory $h$ changes, weights $\theta$ fixed
$h_t = \mathrm{LSTM}_\theta\big(h_{t-1},\ [\,o_t,\ a_{t-1},\ r_{t-1}\,]\big)$
Loop activity folds the last action and
reward into memory (recurrent dynamics)
$a_t \sim \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid h_t)$
Act from memory: explore early,
exploit once the better arm is clear
$r_t,\ o_{t+1} = \mathrm{env}_\tau(a_t)$
Task returns reward and next observation
Outer loop, after each episode: weights $\theta$ change
$\delta_t = R_t - V_\theta(h_t)$
RPE, broadcast as phasic dopamine
($R_t$: n-step return)
$\theta \leftarrow \theta + \alpha\, \delta_t\, \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid h_t) + \dots$
A3C: dopamine adjusts PFC and striatum
synapses, a small step per episode
Test: freeze $\theta$, sample a new $\tau$. Behaviour still improves over trials, so it lives in $h$.

g.text: Left hemisphere（左半球）, seen from the left
VTA / SNc（中脑多巴胺神经元）
PFC + striatum + thalamus = the LSTM; its activity is the memory $h$
Dopamine $\delta_t$ updates the loop synapses $\theta$ after each episode, never $h$:
Brain: a local rule at each synapse, $\Delta w \propto \delta_t \times \text{pre} \times \text{post}$ (no backprop)
$a_{t-1}$ reaches PFC as an efference copy（传出副本）of its own last action

svg.text: What is actually learned?
Weights $\theta$: changed by dopamine (A3C) after each episode
The recipe: how to fold $(a, r)$ into memory and act on it. Fixed at test.
Memory $h$: activity of the PFC loop, changes every trial
This task's answer, e.g. “the right arm pays more”. Erased at the next episode.
Seen from outside, the inner loop is just a fixed policy with memory:
$a_t \sim \pi_\theta\big(\cdot \mid h_t\big),\qquad h_t = f_\theta\big(o_{\le t},\ a_{<t},\ r_{<t}\big)$
The task $\tau$ is a hidden variable of the meta-environment. Within an episode,
“learning” = inferring $\tau$ from the history of actions and rewards.
Caveat: the paper calls this a “second RL algorithm”. Unlike PPO, it cannot train another
network, and it only works on tasks from $p(\tau)$. Learned weight-update rules: LPG, DiscoRL.
